reason: Conversation 1 reaches the most likely cause (overheat protection from the new drawer restricting airflow) quickly, keeps it honestly hedged, and gives a safe interim instruction to stop using high power, though it fails to escalate to the installer/engineer when the homeowner refuses to check under the hob and never asks about the flashing code. Conversation 2 asks sensible questions (code, pans) and does escalate, but its final answer drifts to an unsupported internal-fault story ('heat sink blocked with dust', 'replace the faulty part') that abandons the strong drawer-ventilation clue, suggests 'lifting the hob slightly', and inserts an irrelevant replacement-model panel. Neither is complete, but Conversation 1's diagnosis is more accurate and makes no unsupported part claims.
